title: Pool activity timeline prototype notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc collects UX notes and early wireframe descriptions for an activity timeline view for Dedicated GPU pools. Goal: give capacity owners a single glanceable surface to understand past usage, near-term commitments, and forecasted contention so they can adjust reservations, autoscale rules, and burst budgets proactively.

Why a timeline?
- Current pool UI surfaces are table-heavy (allocations, reservations, capacity by GPU type). Operators repeatedly ask: "what happened last night that spiked eviction?" and "are we going to hit contention tomorrow at 10am?"
- Timeline lets you correlate API usage (requests/min), running instances, queued reservations, and autoscale actions along a single time axis.

High-level components (wireframe building blocks):
1) Global time selector (top-left)
   - Quick ranges: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d
   - Live mode toggle (auto-scroll to live)
   - Custom range with granular step (15m min resolution)
2) Pool selector row
   - Dropdown to switch pools, chip-style filters (GPU type, zone, tier)
   - Small badge showing SLA tier and reserved commit (e.g., "SLA: gold • 8 GPUs reserved")
3) Stacked lanes area (main):
   - Lane A: Request ingress (lines: RPS, percent change)
   - Lane B: Active machines (stacked area by instance type: A100/RTX)
   - Lane C: Reservations and reservations queue (blocks show reservation name, owner; hatch pattern = tentative)
   - Lane D: Autoscale events (vertical ticks show scale-up/scale-down with hover cards)
   - Lane E: Cost burn estimate overlay (semi-transparent)
4) Forecast overlay
   - Dotted projection lines from now → +48h based on historical pattern + current active commitments
   - Confidence band (low/medium/high) derived from workload variance setting (see details below)
5) Contention alert bar (top of timeline)
   - Summarizes predicted hotspots in the window (e.g., "Tomorrow 09:00–11:30: 98% chance of queueing for low-priority work")

Micro-interactions and hover states:
- Hover any reservation block: show name, owner, Jira key (if linked), reservation policy (preemptible? yes/no), ability to jump to reservation edit. CTA: "Request swap" (propose time shift to owner).
- Click a vertical autoscale tick: open mini-trace showing triggering metric values and the decision path (why we scaled). Link out to the autoscale rule editor.
- Drag on the forecast band to propose a temporary burst: creates a draft burst request modal prefilled with start/end and GPU count.

Keyboard & accessibility notes:
- Timeline should be navigable with left/right arrows to move time focus; Enter opens contextual detail; Escape closes modals.
- Color choices: avoid red/green for owner/reservation states; use texture (hatch) for tentative/reserved. Provide colorblind-friendly palette. Provide aria-labels for each lane and each event.

Edge cases and failure modes to design for:
- Long-running reservations that cross multiple time ranges: show condensed caret with "+2d" indicator; allow click-to-expand.
- Overlapping reservations from different teams: stack by priority and render a conflict stripe to encourage edit.
- Missing telemetry (gaps in request ingress): render gray dashed line with tooltip describing data gap and link to SRE runbook for metric ingestion.

Forecasting details (UX-visible knobs):
- Workload variance slider (low/med/high) visible near forecast toggle. Low = optimistic bound (assumes similar pattern); High = conservative, expands confidence band.
- Burst buffer toggle: include current burst credits remaining; clicking opens simple burn-rate calculator (how many credits used for x GPUs for y hours).

Backlog grooming (initial items, estimates in story points):
- CON-771: Render stacked lanes + time selector (5pts) — Asha (owner)
- CON-772: Reservation block interactions + edit jump (3pts) — Jin
- CON-773: Forecast projection algorithm hook & UI (8pts; needs applied-ml input) — Luca
- CON-774: Burst proposal drag-to-create modal (5pts) — Nora
- CON-775: Accessibility pass + keyboard nav (3pts) — Jin
- CON-776: Conflict visualization for overlapping reservations (3pts) — Asha
- CON-777: Export timeline slice as CSV/PNG (2pts) — UX fudge
Notes: CON-773 needs collaboration with applied-ml for the projection confidence bands. Blocker until basic model + API available.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Should reservations created via drag be immediately auto-proposed to owners or first create a local draft with shareable link? (pref: draft + shareable link, reduces accidental notifications)
- How to show private metadata (customer PII) in hovercards for sensitive pools (private deployments)? Proposal: redact by default, allow "view sensitive" for users with permission scope.
- Policy for preemption visualization: when a tentative preemption is forecast, do we mark the lower-priority reservation as "at risk" and notify owners? Need product legal review for automated notifications to external customers.

Example flows (sketch notes):
1) On-call SRE sees red badge indicating predicted contention at 09:00 tomorrow. They open timeline → hover the cost band → identify which migrating batch job is expected to start. They drag a burst request for 4 GPUs 09:00–11:00 and hit "Draft & Share". Owner of the batch job gets a Slack proposal (link to timeline slice).
2) Capacity manager wants weekly trend: switch to 7d range, toggle forecast, export CSV to attach to exec capacity review.

Mock microcopy / labels (for designers to pick up):
- "Predicted contention" badge: "Potential queueing • 95% confidence"
- Reservation badges: "Commit: 4 GPUs • owner: infra-team • preemptible"
- Autoscale tick hover: "Scaled up 8 → 12 • triggered by 99th percentile latency breach (0.9s)"

Implementation notes for infra/engineering:
- Frontend: use existing timeseries canvas (chart-lib) + custom lane renderer. Avoid full DOM for event-heavy renders — canvas with overlayed HTML tooltips recommended.
- Backend: new /pools/{id}/timeline API that returns event series (compact array of timestamped events) and a projection endpoint /pools/{id}/timeline/forecast with optional variance param.
- Permissions: timeline respects pool-level read scopes. Draft proposals saved to /pools/{id}/proposals.

Links & references:
- Linked JIRA ticket: CON-771 (master tracking)
- Confluence spec stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CON/Pool+Activity+Timeline+spec
- Slack thread: #console-ux thread id (see messages CON-UX-2025-02-08)

Notes to self (ASAP):
- Schedule 30m sync with Applied ML (Luca) to confirm projection input data + cadence.
- Prototype basic lane stacking in Storybook — aim for interactive drag by end of next sprint.
- Add small usability test (5 users) to validate whether timeline layout reduces time-to-detect contention vs current table view.

Unresolved / future enhancements:
- Integrate model-level traces (token-level timeline) into a second zoom layer for debugging latency spikes tied to specific models.
- Add "what-if" mode where operators can simulate hypothetical reservations and see cost/latency impact without creating drafts.

End of notes.

Version history:
- 2025-02-10 initial draft by Asha
- 2025-02-13 added forecast knobs and backlog items (Luca)
- 2025-02-18 updated interactions and accessibility checklist (Jin)
